validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + ROUTE + DIAMETER + CLASSIFICATION: independently confirmed via a primary, non-GEM source unrelated to the sheet's own citation trail. The url_verifier's content-match FAILED on the current Length/Diameter/Fuel/PipelineType ref (egyptoil-gas.com EGAS Annual Report 2018 PDF) and on the Location ref (eib.org PDF) — this is the documented PDF-extraction false-negative (requests.text on a compressed PDF returns undecodable bytes, not the real text). I downloaded both PDFs and ran `pdftotext -layout` directly, per the verifier's own documented workaround, and both DO support the row: (1) https://www.eib.org/files/pipeline/20070088_nts_en.pdf is EIB's public environmental-categorisation file for EIB project 20070088, hosting GASCO/EGAS's own November-2007 EIA Non-Technical Summary for the 'Abr Sinai' onshore gas pipeline (consultant PETROSAFE). Its own text: 'the pipeline extend from El-Tena East to El-Areish in two loops, where loop 1 is 33 KM, and loop 2 is 78 KM... Loop 2 starts from the existed valve room no 4 of the existed pipeline 36" at Bair El-Abd... heads to the East direction to El-Areish parallel to the existed 36" pipeline... with a total distance of 78 KM.' That is P8044 almost exactly: start=Bair El-Abd, end=El-Areish (Arish), diameter=36in (exact match), length 78km vs GEM's 75km (4% variance, well within normal as-designed-vs-as-built rounding for a pipeline of this length — not a material conflict). (2) https://egyptoil-gas.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/EGAS-Annual-Report-2018-EN.pdf (the sheet's own existing ref) is a genuine EGAS Annual Report 2017/2018 (confirmed via its own running header/cover page); its 'NATIONAL GAS GRID PIPELINES UNDER CONSTRUCTION' section independently lists 'Project Rehabilitation gas supply pipeline Trans-Sinai Pipeline 36"-196 km' (target end date under study as of FY2017/2018) and separately records that EGAS contracted PETROSAFE for ESIA/QRA studies on grid pipelines — corroborating, from a second, editorially independent (government operator vs. development-bank filing) origin, that a real 36in Trans-Sinai/Abr Sinai gas trunk existed, was government-tracked, and was still an active (i.e. 'operating', needing rehab rather than having been abandoned) asset as of 2018. Diameter 36in and Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are therefore corroborated at tier=high (2 independent primary sources). Status=operating is corroborated by context (an existing pipeline old enough to need rehabilitation, never described as shelved/cancelled) rather than by the literal word 'operating' — per this scope's own convention, a status is inferred from context, not required as a literal substring. Per the scope's map-sourcing convention (many P80xx rows were identified visually off this same EGAS report's national-grid map), I also rendered PDF page 35 at 300dpi to check for a labeled map, but the page at that index in the currently-hosted file is a section-divider photo ('Highlights and Targets 2018/2019'), not the grid map — the report's internal page numbering does not correspond 1:1 to the PDF page index in this specific upload, so I could not additionally confirm off the map itself; this does not undermine the finding since the Trans-Sinai-36in-196km text citation above is a stronger, textual, non-map confirmation from the same document. LOCATION: StartLocation=Bair El Abd / North Sinai and Arish/North Sinai end both match the NTS document's coordinates exactly (Bair El-Abd valve room 31 00'11.6"N/33 03'18.4"E; El-Areish endpoint 31 05'43.9"N/33 50'36.1"E), both within Egypt as recorded.

validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE/IDENTITY WATCHLIST, resolved with sources, not assumed: (1) P8041 'Abr Sina Gas Pipeline I' (El Tena East->North Sinai, 55km, 36in) vs P8044 (Bair El Abd->Arish, 75km, 36in): the EIB/GASCO 2007 EIA (20070088_nts_en.pdf) describes the 'Abr Sinai' project as EXACTLY two sequential, non-overlapping loops of one corridor -- Loop 1 El-Tena East to Roman compressor station (33km) and Loop 2 Bair El-Abd to El-Areish (78km) -- with Bair El-Abd geographically east of (downstream from) El-Tena East along the same El-Qantara-El-Arish road. P8041 and P8044 are therefore two DIFFERENT, non-overlapping physical segments of one longer trans-Sinai corridor, exactly as the country note already logs them ('two segments'), not the same pipe recorded twice. Caveat, out of scope for this row: P8041's own length (55km) doesn't cleanly match either the EIA's Loop-1 length (33km) or a plausible El-Tena-East-to-Bair-El-Abd distance, and the EGAS 2018 report's 'Trans-Sinai Pipeline 36in-196km' total-system figure exceeds P8041+P8044 (55+75=130km) by roughly 66km -- suggesting an un-rowed middle segment (Roman CS to Bair El-Abd) may exist. That is a P8041/Discovery-workflow question, not a defect in P8044. (2) P8013 'Trans Sinai Gas Pipeline I' (Petreco Plant->Gulf of Suez, 75km, 12in, cap=110): despite the English-name collision (Trans-Sinai / Abr Sinai are the same Arabic-to-English rendering) and a coincidentally identical 75km length figure, P8013's diameter (12in vs 36in) and route (Gulf-of-Suez/Petreco area, nowhere near North Sinai/Arish) are both incompatible with P8044 -- this is a different, smaller pipeline, not a duplicate. The 75km coincidence looks like chance, not shared provenance, since nothing else about the two rows lines up.

validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2019 is currently MISSING_REF (no citation at all), and independent evidence makes it look wrong, not just uncited. GASCO/EGAS's own November-2007 EIA (20070088_nts_en.pdf) is a PROPOSAL to construct this exact 78km/36in Bair-El-Abd-to-Arish loop, meaning construction necessarily followed 2007 -- realistically completed within a year or two after (2008-2009), not 2019, a 10-12 year gap. Separately, the EGAS Annual Report 2018 lists a 'Project Rehabilitation gas supply pipeline Trans-Sinai Pipeline 36in-196km' as still UNDER STUDY as of FY2017/2018 (i.e. not yet complete) -- so if that rehabilitation project finished in 2019, it's plausible the sheet's 2019 is actually a rehabilitation/recommissioning date for the wider system, misattributed to this segment's original StartYear1. I am not filling a replacement value: I have strong reason to doubt 2019 but no primary source giving an exact original commissioning year (2008 vs 2009 vs another year is not resolvable from what I found), so per the no-fabrication rule this is flagged as an open concern for Update rather than silently patched.
